subject: Literature
subcategory: Classic Novels That Changed the World
title: The Rights of Man and Democratic Thought
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Rights of Man and Democratic Thought.

hook.text: When Edmund Burke attacked the French Revolution, Thomas Paine wrote a furious defense of human rights.

buildup.text: The Rights of Man argued that every generation has the right to choose its own government freely.

discovery.text: The book sold over a million copies in England, terrifying the British monarchy and Parliament.

twist.text: Paine was charged with treason and fled to France, where he was later imprisoned during the Terror.

climax.text: His ideas influenced democratic constitutions around the world for the next two centuries.

punchline.text: A fugitive's book shaped democracies for centuries.

quiz.question: What happened to Thomas Paine after writing The Rights of Man?
options: He became Prime Minister of England
He was charged with treason and fled to France
